significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) ordering claim that an LLM "first retrieves the affirmative fact" in mid layers and "only afterward attempts to suppress or invert" it in late layers, together with the causal coupling that negation errors occur when this override fails. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing the temporal relationship between factual retrieval and polarity integration rather than merely identifying a decodable direction; that relationship would connect the behavioral negation failures documented by Kassner and Schütze (2020) and Ettinger (2020) to the enrichment-then-extraction account of factual recall in Geva et al. (2023). Verified false would meaningfully rule out retrieve-then-override as a general explanation, although it would not identify which competing mechanism is correct; true and false are therefore distinct, informative states. In the topic-substitution check, the broad topic of knowledge retrieval alone would not earn this score: the claim-specific ordering of retrieval before negation, which is false of a median localization hypothesis, supplies the added weight.

reach.justification: The claim hands downstream users two named handles: an "example-level diagnostic distinguishing 'retrieved-but-failed-to-negate' from other errors" and a training-free "negation-completion" intervention that suppresses the retrieved affirmative direction. The diagnostic is explicitly ex ante because it predicts "before the answer" whether override failure will occur, while the intervention provides an inference-time action window rather than only explaining an error afterward. Although the suppression direction may require re-extraction, the retrieve-mid-layer/override-late ordering is a transferable relation that predicts what researchers should find across model families and scales; the likely downstream users include model auditors and developers gating or correcting negated-query responses, though the asserted scope is limited mainly to factual and category-based negation. Under topic substitution, generic knowledge-retrieval research would not itself provide either the pre-answer failure predictor or the corrective intervention, so the reach score comes from these claim-specific handles rather than the topic's breadth.
